diagnosis: The bot is roughly break-even overall (50.7% win rate, -$68.37 over 404 trades) but the aggregate masks a clear bimodal split: ARB setups are strongly profitable (92% win, +$5.89 over 13 trades) while MOMENTUM, the dominant strategy (383/404 trades), is a net loser (49% win, -$55.81). Within momentum, the lesson-bucket data pinpoints the leak precisely: moves in the 10-20bps range are catastrophic (-$33.47 over 81 trades, 34.6% win) and entries with <45c price are bad (-$19.54, 30.6% win), while moves <10bps are mildly negative (-$5.55, 48% win) and 20+bps moves are strongly positive (+$10.14, 55.8% win). Time-to-expiry also matters: left60-120s is a loser (-$20.25, 35.6% win) and left<60s is a disaster (-$19.40, 15.4% win, small sample), while left120+ is the only profitable time bucket (+$10.77, 50.3% win). Coin-level data shows btc-updown is the only clearly profitable coin (+$10.83, 60% win) while doge-updown is the worst (-$23.45, 39% win). The veto system is already correctly identifying and blocking move10-20 setups in recent decisions (many SKIPs), which is good, but the bot is still entering low-quality setups like the eth-updown-5m-1790894600 one with ask=0.55 and only 0.6-0.7bps edge relative to a 9.5bps move in a mid price band that the 'price0.55-0.70' bucket shows is marginally negative (-$7.21, 51% expectancy -0.086). The all-agree peer consensus bucket is surprisingly negative (-$18.99, 44.6% win) suggesting the peer-agreement signal is not adding value and may even be a false-confidence trap, while some-agree is also mildly negative. Stop-losses are firing very late/deep (0.19-0.25 bid) causing large losses per trade (worst trade -$15.93), while take-profits cap gains modestly (~0.90-0.93). This asymmetry (big stop losses, small take profits) combined with ~50% win rate structurally destroys edge even when win rate is near breakeven.
priorityActions: 1) Escalate left<60s bucket to hard veto immediately given -$19.40 P&L / 15.4% win rate on small but severe sample.
2) Raise min_entry_left_sec toward 150s to structurally avoid late entries rather than relying solely on post-hoc veto filtering.
3) Investigate and address the 'all-agree' peer-consensus paradox (-$18.99 P&L, 44.6% win) — this is the largest-sample lesson anomaly and likely degrading the core momentum signal.
4) Increase max_open_positions to 2 to better capture rare but high-edge ARB setups without displacing momentum trades.
5) Resolve the balance-read/telemetry integrity issue (17,948 bad reads) before trusting further live-learned lesson updates or increasing trade size.
6) Consider a coin-specific confidence/edge penalty for doge-updown given its persistent underperformance relative to btc-updown.
